prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original SNES title-screen background plate
Primary request: an original 16-bit arcade fighting-game backdrop for a 256x224 pixel-art title screen, designed to be reduced with nearest-neighbor sampling
Scene/backdrop: a dramatic Santiago, Chile evening skyline with layered Andes silhouettes, a broad dark navy sky, a few geometric office-tower shapes, subtle rooftop antennae, and a low horizon band that leaves clean dark negative space in the central upper-middle area for code-authored logo text
Subject: environment only, no people, no fighters
Style/medium: hand-painted cartoon arcade background, bold clean shapes, limited color blocks, crisp edges, 1990s console game key-art mood, no photorealism
Composition/framing: wide 3:2 landscape, skyline low in frame, strong diagonal cloud and light streak accents, uncluttered center and lower-center areas for overlay typography and menu UI
Lighting/mood: electric twilight, warm sunset rim on the Andes and buildings, deep blue-violet shadows, energetic but readable
Color palette: deep navy, indigo, cyan, teal, violet, hot magenta accents, sunset gold and orange
Materials/textures: subtle halftone and hand-painted brush texture that survives pixel reduction, layered silhouettes, a few tiny window lights
Text (verbatim): ""
Constraints: original artwork with no logos, no signage, no legible text, no watermark, no copied game assets; keep the central negative space calm for a title overlay
Avoid: photorealism, 3D render, realistic faces, detailed crowds, excessive neon glow, busy text-like marks, generic cyberpunk city, Capcom or Street Fighter branding

source_validation.native_crop: Pillow ImageOps.fit to 256x224, LANCZOS, centering=(0.5,0.43), then darkened and palette-authored by tools/menu_assets.py
source_validation.text_policy: No generated text is used; all title and menu text is authored with the project's pixel glyph callback.
